question: Can general-domain replay during multimodal RLVR preserve capabilities that narrow reasoning fine-tuning erodes, while an online scalar-history scheduler allocates weight among heterogeneous reasoning, perception, OCR, and format objectives without proxy models or per-task gradients?

key_findings.claim: Reasoning post-training can cause skill-specific regression, but the controlled Qwen2.5-VL-7B experiment does not show broad degradation across all measured general capabilities.
key_findings.evidence: Relative to the base model, reasoning-only fine-tuning drops LISA segmentation from 65.13 to 57.58 and OCRBenchv2 from 39.49 to 38.55, while improving the other seven Table 2 benchmarks, sometimes substantially. Figure 1 also shows several public reasoning-tuned models below their base counterparts, but those pairs use heterogeneous undisclosed training recipes. The evidence supports selective perception/OCR forgetting, not uniform loss of general knowledge or the abstract's unmeasured faithfulness claim.

key_findings.claim: RECAP combines explicit replay with online softmax weighting based on two adjacent loss windows: relative decrease c_k = old_mean/current_mean and instability i_k = window_std/(current_mean+old_mean).
key_findings.evidence: After 2W observations per objective, it sets a score from c and i, applies temperature-softmax weights normalized to mean one, and minimizes the weighted average loss. The entropy theorem proves only that softmax is the optimizer of a linear score plus entropy; it does not establish that these scores optimize retention or Pareto performance.

key_findings.claim: In the 3B RLVR-only setting, RECAP outperforms both Uniform and the expensive static-mixture MoDoMoDo baseline on five of six benchmarks and ties MoDoMoDo on ChartQA.
key_findings.evidence: RECAP scores 55.19 SAT, 71.59 ScienceQA, 33.2 MathVista-mini, 70.40 ChartQA, 60.78 InfoVQA, and 42.44 MMMU. Uniform scores 44.55, 64.85, 32.4, 69.68, 58.30, and 39.44; MoDoMoDo scores 49.95, 65.74, 32.2, 70.40, 59.88, and 39.11. No seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests accompany the table.

key_findings.claim: In the 7B hybrid setting, RECAP improves every reported benchmark over the same-pipeline Uniform baseline and recovers the two capabilities degraded by reasoning-only training while retaining similar reasoning scores.
key_findings.evidence: Against Uniform, RECAP changes LISA 65.18->67.24, MMMU-Pro 31.91->34.15, AI2D 76.43->78.21, MathVista 65.60->66.70, MathVision 22.13->25.11, MathVerse 36.07->40.83, MMBench 75.34->78.52, VizWiz 54.05->61.97, and OCRBenchv2 38.06->39.72. Against reasoning-only, RECAP recovers LISA by 9.66 points and OCRBenchv2 by 1.17 while being within 0.48 point or better on each reported reasoning/general benchmark.

key_findings.claim: The paper's description of the scheduler as prioritizing slow or underperforming objectives conflicts with its convergence-rate equation.
key_findings.evidence: For a positive loss, c_k = old_mean/current_mean is largest when the loss has recently fallen fastest, not when it is improving slowly; a high plateau gives c approximately 1. Page 6 nevertheless says the method steers toward objectives that are 'slow to converge (high c)'. Instability can prioritize volatile objectives, but neither c nor i measures absolute underperformance, so the abstract's shift toward underperforming objectives is not implied by the rule.

key_findings.claim: The exact score used in the experiments is internally inconsistent between the main method/pseudocode and the appendix ablations.
key_findings.evidence: The main text and Algorithm 2 use s=c+i. Appendix A.2 says the experiments use alpha=0.5, and Appendix pages 32-33 define s=alpha*c+(1-alpha)*i and report alpha ablations. At alpha=0.5 this halves every score; with fixed T=5 it is equivalent to c+i at T=10, so it is not an innocuous common scaling under softmax. A second normalization conflict appears on page 10: the main rule defines mean-one lambda and the pseudocode initializes lambda=1, but the Uniform description says lambda_k=1/K. The paper does not resolve which formulas produced Tables 1-2.

anchors.section: A.7, default alpha statement and Table 5

key_findings.claim: Replay plus dynamic weighting shortens generated reasoning traces, but the attribution between replay and weighting is not isolated for this outcome.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 7 reports about 67.3 words per question for reasoning-only fine-tuning versus 27.3 for RECAP, a roughly 60% reduction, alongside comparable benchmark accuracy. Because the comparison changes both the training-data mixture and the weighting scheduler, it cannot show that reweighting itself caused the shorter traces; the paper provides no Uniform trace-length value.

key_findings.claim: Appendix tests show that RECAP is an efficient general multi-task loss balancer, but the strongest efficient predecessors are omitted from the main VLM RLVR tables.
key_findings.evidence: On NYUv2, RECAP records mIoU 41.26, pixel accuracy 66.79, absolute depth error 0.5303, relative error 0.2203, and Delta m 0.77, outperforming the listed O(1) loss-weighting methods on most metrics. The runtime plot reports roughly 100 seconds for scalar-weighting approaches versus roughly 300 seconds for gradient-based methods at K=3. Yet FAMO and DWA—direct efficient dynamic-weighting competitors included in the synthetic/NYUv2 appendix—are not evaluated in Tables 1-2, so the VLM evidence isolates RECAP only from static replay and KL baselines.

method.core_idea: Uniformly sample target-reasoning and general-capability replay data, then dynamically reweight their individual objectives using only short loss histories rather than proxy models or per-objective gradients.
method.mechanism: For each objective, RECAP stores 2W recent scalar losses, computes the means of the newest and preceding W steps, forms an old/current loss ratio and a coefficient-of-variation-like instability score, combines them, and applies a temperature softmax normalized so average weight is one. The resulting weighted sum is optimized with the underlying GRPO or SFT update. In the hybrid VLM experiment, reasoning data supplies accuracy and thinking-format objectives, RefCOCO supplies IoU and answer-format objectives, and OCR replay supplies next-token prediction.
assumptions: Each objective exposes a comparable, finite scalar loss every update or has a well-defined aggregation across sampled domains.
Loss-window means and their sum stay away from zero and do not change sign; the pseudocode adds no epsilon or clipping to either ratio.
Two windows of W=10 steps are long enough to smooth on-policy noise but short enough to track non-stationarity.
Uniform domain sampling already supplies an acceptable replay distribution; RECAP reweights objectives rather than learning sample proportions.
Recent relative loss decrease and variability are useful proxies for priority even though neither directly measures held-out retention or task underperformance.
Five objectives in the hybrid setting and eight in the RLVR-only setting adequately represent the capability trade-off.
Results on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B and the chosen vision-language datasets transfer to broader reasoning post-training.

techniques.role: Interleaves perception and OCR examples with the target reasoning data so gradients continue to exercise selected base capabilities.
Uses the ratio of preceding-window to current-window mean loss as a scale-invariant recent-change signal.
Raises weight on objectives whose scalar losses remain variable relative to their recent mean scale.
Turns scalar priorities into positive mean-one objective weights while controlling concentration with temperature.
Avoids storing K separate model gradients, adding only O(KW) scalar history and arithmetic.
Uses thinking-format rewards only for reasoning domains and direct-answer format rewards for perception tasks.

limitations: Author-stated: experiments cover RLVR and standard SFT only; preference optimization, alignment objectives, and process reward models are left to future work.
Author-stated: large RL compute prevented additional hyperparameter tuning in the hybrid setting; alpha=0.5, T=5, and W=10 were carried over from the smaller setup.
Reviewer-identified: the two main model tables report no seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests, so small margins cannot be separated from RL/evaluation variance.
Reviewer-identified: the paper does not specify GPU model, wall time, total tokens, random seeds, or a public code release for RECAP, despite claiming negligible overhead and less compute.

Reviewer-identified: 'general capability' training and evaluation are concentrated on perception, OCR, visual QA, and multimodal reasoning; language, coding, safety, factuality, calibration, and faithfulness retention are not tested.

Reviewer-identified: the controlled reasoning-only model regresses on two of nine Table 2 metrics and improves seven, so the evidence is selective forgetting rather than wholesale general-knowledge loss.

Reviewer-identified: replay data, reward routing, and dynamic weighting change together in some comparisons; Uniform isolates weighting for benchmark scores, but not for trace length or every claimed mechanism.
Reviewer-identified: FAMO and DWA are efficient dynamic-weighting predecessors evaluated only on synthetic/NYUv2 tasks, not in the main VLM RLVR experiments.

Reviewer-identified: main text/pseudocode use s=c+i while experimental details use alpha=0.5 in s=alpha*c+(1-alpha)*i; with softmax this changes the effective temperature and leaves the exact implementation ambiguous.

Reviewer-identified: c and i divide by raw loss means without epsilon, sign handling, clipping, or missing-objective masking; magnitude invariance holds for positive scaling but not additive shifts, negative RL surrogates, or near-zero means.
Reviewer-identified: the entropy theorem is a correct restatement of softmax optimization but gives no learning, retention, convergence, or regret guarantee for RECAP's chosen score.
failure_modes: An objective mean approaching zero makes old/current and standard-deviation/mean ratios explode, causing a single softmax weight to dominate.
Negative or sign-changing policy losses can invert the meaning of both priority signals and make the denominator cross zero.
A high-loss stalled objective with stable windows receives c approximately 1 and i approximately 0, so the scheduler does not actually prioritize an underperforming plateau.
A noisy but unlearnable or corrupted objective can keep high instability and consume training weight indefinitely.
With W too large, reweighting begins after objectives have saturated; with W too small, on-policy noise controls weights.
Low temperature amplifies measurement noise and creates oscillatory task dominance; very high temperature collapses toward Uniform and reacts too slowly.
Replay preserves only capabilities represented in the chosen memory; perception/OCR replay cannot guarantee safety, factuality, language fluency, or other absent skills.
Uniform domain sampling can over- or under-sample domains relative to their diversity and importance even if objective weights adapt afterward.
Dynamic weighting may optimize benchmark-specific format and reward signals while hidden capabilities outside the evaluation panel continue to drift.
reusable_insights: Capability retention during post-training should be measured alongside target-task gains; aggregate reasoning scores can hide regressions in perception or grounding.
Replay and objective weighting are separate controls: sample allocation determines which evidence appears, while loss coefficients determine its gradient influence.
Short-window scalar histories offer a cheap control signal when per-task gradients are unaffordable, but their direction and numerical safeguards must be explicit.
Format objectives often saturate before correctness objectives, so fixed reward weights can keep spending capacity on already-solved constraints.
Reward types should match task needs; forcing long thinking traces on direct perception tasks can produce needless verbosity.
Any claimed magnitude invariance should be tested under scaling, offsets, zero crossings, and negative surrogate losses rather than inferred from ratios alone.
Efficient dynamic schedulers should be compared against other O(1) loss-history methods in the target large-model setting, not only against static mixtures and O(K) gradient methods.
open_questions: Which exact score—c+i or alpha*c+(1-alpha)*i—generated the reported tables, and do results reproduce across seeds?
Can the ratios be made numerically safe and directionally correct for signed RL objectives, missing task losses, and objectives whose optimum is zero?
Would prioritizing held-out retention deficits or regret, rather than recent training-loss decrease, better serve the stated goal of preserving underperforming capabilities?
How does RECAP compare with FAMO, DWA, GradNorm approximations, and learned bandit schedulers in the same Qwen RLVR runs under equal compute?
How much of the gain comes from replay data, domain sampling, task-specific format routing, the c signal, and the i signal across multiple seeds?
Does RECAP preserve text-only knowledge, safety, factual grounding, calibration, and faithfulness under prolonged RLVR?
How do results scale beyond Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B, beyond 500 steps, and to preference/process-reward post-training?
Can a scheduler provide a Pareto, no-regret, or lower-bound retention guarantee while retaining scalar-history efficiency?

competitive_landscape.title: MoDoMoDo: Multi-Domain Data Mixtures for Multimodal LLM Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Closest static multi-domain multimodal-RLVR competitor and the paper's stated upper-bound baseline.
competitive_landscape.difference: MoDoMoDo fits proxy models to predict held-out RL performance as a function of domain sample proportions, then selects a fixed mixture. RECAP samples domains uniformly and adapts per-objective coefficients online from one model's short loss history, avoiding proxy training but not optimizing the data mixture itself.

competitive_landscape.title: RLEP: Reinforcement Learning with Experience Replay for LLM Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct experience-replay competitor for stabilizing reasoning RL and limiting policy drift.
competitive_landscape.difference: RLEP collects verified successful reasoning trajectories and mixes them with new rollouts to improve convergence and final math accuracy. RECAP replays heterogeneous general-capability data for retention and dynamically balances several losses; it does not preferentially replay verified successes.

competitive_landscape.title: SRFT: A Single-Stage Method with Supervised and Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent hybrid SFT-plus-RL objective-balancing method for reasoning post-training.
competitive_landscape.difference: SRFT jointly uses demonstrations and self-exploration rollouts with entropy-aware weighting to improve mathematical reasoning. RECAP's hybrid setting instead targets general-capability retention with explicit perception/OCR replay and windowed convergence/instability weights.

competitive_landscape.title: Perception-Aware Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct multimodal-RL competitor addressing perception loss during reasoning optimization.
competitive_landscape.difference: PAPO adds an implicit-perception KL objective and double-entropy regularization without extra curated replay data, directly coupling visual grounding to the policy objective. RECAP uses explicit perception/OCR examples and a generic scheduler across rewards and SFT losses.

competitive_landscape.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
competitive_landscape.relationship: Canonical post-training retention predecessor using both reference regularization and pretraining replay.
competitive_landscape.difference: InstructGPT's PPO-ptx variant mixes pretraining gradients into RLHF and uses a KL penalty to reduce public-benchmark regression. RECAP generalizes the replay idea to selected VLM capability domains and adapts multiple objective weights online rather than using fixed PPO/pretraining coefficients.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning without Forgetting
competitive_landscape.relationship: Foundational functional-regularization baseline for preserving old capabilities.
competitive_landscape.difference: LwF preserves outputs on old tasks by distilling the original model using only new-task data, whereas RECAP assumes access to replay examples from old/general domains and adjusts their objectives online. The paper's LwF-labeled baseline is a reference-policy KL variant under uniform sampling rather than a complete reproduction of every original LwF detail.

competitive_landscape.title: FAMO: Fast Adaptive Multitask Optimization
competitive_landscape.difference: FAMO already uses loss dynamics to balance task improvement with O(1) model-scale space/time and evaluates supervised and reinforcement-learning tasks. RECAP's narrower mechanism novelty is two-window relative decrease plus explicit instability and its application to replay-based multimodal RLVR; FAMO is not tested in the main VLM tables.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 36 (2023) Main Conference, official proceedings final

competitive_landscape.title: GradNorm: Gradient Normalization for Adaptive Loss Balancing in Deep Multitask Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: GradNorm downweights fast-training tasks and upweights slow ones by explicitly balancing per-task gradient magnitudes and relative training rates. RECAP avoids K model-gradient computations and uses only scalar windows, but its old/current ratio actually grows for faster recent loss decrease, so it does not implement GradNorm's stated slow-task direction.
competitive_landscape.source_version: PMLR volume 80, ICML 2018, pages 794-803 (official proceedings final)

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a plug-in, magnitude-agnostic replay scheduler that uses short-horizon convergence and instability to move RLVR training away from saturated objectives toward underperforming or volatile ones, preserving general capabilities without auxiliary models or heavy tuning.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Primary competitors cover pretraining replay, functional distillation, verified reasoning replay, static learned domain mixtures, perception-specific KL objectives, hybrid SFT/RL, gradient-rate balancing, and efficient loss-history weighting. RECAP's distinct combination is heterogeneous general-capability replay plus a two-window decrease/instability softmax evaluated in multimodal RLVR and hybrid SFT.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The application-level combination and the same-pipeline gains over Uniform are useful and appear new, but replay, dynamic weighting, training-rate signals, softmax/entropy allocation, and O(1)-scale loss-history methods are all prior. Novelty narrows further because FAMO is a close efficient scheduler absent from the main VLM comparison, the c ratio does not prioritize slow objectives as claimed, and the paper conflicts on whether experimental scores use c+i or alpha=0.5. The evidence supports a promising heuristic for selected VLM retention, not a generic or theoretically justified solution to general-capability forgetting.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review covered all 33 pages of arXiv:2510.21978v2: the public-model audit, equations and entropy proof, both VLM tables, all appendix data/training details, algorithms and pseudocode, qualitative rollouts, reward dynamics, objective coefficients, synthetic Pareto study, NYUv2 table, runtime plot, and alpha/temperature/window ablations. The indexed PDF pin was independently checked on 2026-08-23 by downloading https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.21978v2; its SHA-256 exactly matched 95a15ab1a68fb3f83faa5243a5602215a290dd8d6df4a902ec50d0882672ce27. The local extract covers 33/33 pages. All table values and negative results were retained, including reasoning-only gains on seven of nine hybrid metrics, Coreset wins on three columns, alpha/temperature/window trade-offs, and instability when either score component is used alone. Eight exact official primary competitor records were opened and version-pinned on 2026-08-23.
